tasks.short: Explain products, prices and product use.

steps.what: Look up the current product price, specification and permitted offer conditions
Explain products or services and prices and answer customer questions
Demonstrate use of products safely and respond to the customer's reaction

tasks.design: Use the native searchable catalogue category of {OTHER}, with an offline price view where needed. Only repeated lookup changes; explanation, demonstration and response to customers remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper or scattered catalogue material makes occasional price and condition lookup slow.
tasks.enabler_now: A native mobile catalogue can keep current product identifiers and approved details together.
tasks.still_hard: Customers may misunderstand use, limitations or total price.
tasks.human_edge: Explain honestly and adapt a physical demonstration to the person.
tasks.altitude: A small lookup benefit; selling skill and customer interaction remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: mobile catalogues can support current price and specification lookup without replacing explanation or physical demonstration.

assumptions: Boundary includes genuine product-detail lookup, explanation and demonstration. Order capture and payment are distinct tasks below, not hidden in conversation. No written quote or follow-up is assumed here. Shares are provisional.

The merchandise owner supplies product ID, description, approved price, validity dates, taxes and offer conditions. s1 checks the selected item and expiry; missing or stale information is verified manually before explanation.
Test native catalogue and offline views first. No saving is credited when sellers already know the details or use an equivalent view. No system records customer conversations or generates claims.
No send or record commitment occurs in this read-only support design. The physical demonstration and all customer-facing judgement retain full time.
research_questions: Is any repeated price lookup left after existing seller tools?

incremental.description: Check catalogue freshness and offline synchronization

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes three lookup hours less half an hour of upkeep. Low assumes an equivalent native view already exists, leaving upkeep only. Ninety-five hours of explanation and demonstration remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Deliver the agreed merchandise and check the items with the customer
Enter the merchandise and amount to collect in the mobile point-of-sale terminal
Approve the exact payment amount, merchandise and selected payment method
Collect payment from the customer by card or cash and check the result
Approve the final payment record and receipt against actual funds received
Record the approved collected payment against the merchandise sale
Give the customer the approved merchandise payment receipt

tasks.design: Configure native item selection and payment recording in the mobile-point-of-sale category of {OTHER}. Keep physical delivery and collection human, with distinct checks before collecting the exact amount and before committing the resulting payment and giving its receipt.
tasks.previous_blocker: The seller repeats item details and later copies payment results into sales records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native item lookup and payment-to-sale linking can reduce those entries.
tasks.still_hard: Cash discrepancies, failed card payments and disputed deliveries require direct resolution.
tasks.human_edge: Verify actual delivery and actual payment without treating a pending transaction as received funds.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated entry; delivery, cash handling and payment checks remain unchanged.

reach.task: Resolve failed payment and receipt discrepancies

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: mobile point-of-sale tools can reuse item details and link payment results to sale records; physical delivery and cash verification remain human.

assumptions: Boundary includes delivery, payment capture, collection, recording and receipt handover. Customer time and payment-network runtime are excluded; all shares are seller labour and provisional.

Agreed sale details come from the already captured order or seller's direct item selection. s2 counts barcode/item selection, quantity entry and any agreed-price exception; no free structured sales input is assumed.

Card terminal supplies transaction ID, amount, status and timestamp. For cash, the seller records amount received and change during s4; s5 checks actual tender. Receipt draft is generated from these existing point-of-sale fields in s4, before final approval.

Test native point-of-sale payment linking first. Original order entry is not duplicated here; s2 is the collection interface's repeated entry only where it actually occurs. No saved physical time or payment success increase is claimed. Changes void the matching action's approval.
research_questions: Does native linking remove duplicate payment entry while preserving failed-payment and cash checks?

already_counted.description: Approve amount and method before collection
Check actual payment and approve final record and receipt

approvals.approved_version: Exact merchandise, amount and tender method approved in s3; changes require reapproval
Actual payment-result snapshot and sale mapping approved in s5; changed status or amount voids approval
Exact final receipt and customer sale approved in s5; edits require renewed approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High: four repeated-item-entry hours saved less one upkeep. Low: native sale linking already operates and upkeep remains. Same-sale payment commitment, delivery, collection and receipt handover retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Capture the customer's merchandise selection, quantities and delivery details
Look up merchandise identifiers, prices and available delivery choices
Confirm merchandise, quantities and delivery information with the customer
Calculate order totals, permitted discounts and delivery charges
Approve the complete merchandise order and verified customer delivery information
Record the approved merchandise order in the sales order system

tasks.design: Configure native mobile order entry in the sales-order category of {OTHER}. Capture once at the customer, use catalogue rules for totals, and commit only the reviewed final order; no model interprets the customer's intent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper capture, catalogue lookup and later entry repeat the same merchandise details.
tasks.enabler_now: Native mobile item forms and fixed price rules can remove repeated writing and arithmetic.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous product choices, delivery exceptions and price disputes require customer clarification.
tasks.human_edge: Confirm what the customer actually wants and explain the complete cost.
tasks.altitude: Less transcription; the seller still confirms and accepts each order.

reach.task: Verify exact product variants and identifiers

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: mobile order forms can reuse catalogue fields, calculate fixed totals and record approved orders; ambiguous choices require human confirmation.

assumptions: Boundary is merchandise order capture through internal recording. Payment and delivery are separate tasks; no customer confirmation send is proposed. Shares are provisional for a paper-to-system workflow.

s1 captures product selection, quantity, customer name and delivery details from the customer's actual request, manually on a native form in the future; this input labour remains counted. s2 maps exact product IDs and handles missing variants manually.

Merchandise owners supply price, tax, discount permissions and delivery-charge rules with validity dates. s3 confirms details and corrections in retained time. s4 uses only configured rules; out-of-rule discounts return to seller clarification before s5.

Test native mobile forms and offline synchronization first. Missing addresses or stale prices block commitment. No unverified address structuring is assumed. The final draft exists before s5, and any changed field invalidates s6 approval.
research_questions: Can capture-once remove transcription without shifting address correction to fulfilment staff?

incremental.description: Maintain catalogue rules and reconcile offline synchronization failures

approvals.approved_version: Exact final merchandise, quantity, price, delivery details and customer mapping approved in s5; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High: twelve transcription, nine lookup and fifteen arithmetic hours saved less two upkeep. Low: direct entry and native totals already cover those mechanics. Same-order-system commitment and customer confirmation retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange buying parties and solicit host sponsorship.

steps.what: Solicit sponsorship of buying parties through conversation with potential hosts
Agree buying-party date, location, merchandise and host responsibilities
Draft the host confirmation and party booking details
Approve the final host confirmation and complete party booking
Send the approved buying-party confirmation to the host
Record the approved buying-party booking in the seller's calendar

tasks.design: Use native {EMAIL} templates and {CALENDAR} booking fields around human host conversations. Draft the complete confirmation and booking together, then apply separate final-version gates to host delivery and internal calendar recording.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreed arrangements are copied into both host messages and calendar bookings.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates can reuse fixed party information and the same captured arrangement fields.
tasks.still_hard: Hosts need trust, realistic expectations and genuine agreement on responsibilities.
tasks.human_edge: Build a willing host relationship without pressuring people into commitments.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated arrangement handling; host solicitation and negotiation retain full time.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: message templates and native calendar fields can reduce repeated arrangement copying without replacing host recruitment or agreement.

assumptions: Boundary includes sponsorship conversation, party arrangements, written confirmation and calendar recording; it does not include the selling event itself. Shares are provisional.

Host supplies preferences and agreed responsibilities in s1 and s2. Seller manually captures date, time, venue, host name, reply address, expected merchandise and agreed terms in s3's retained time; no structured party record is free.

s3 reuses only approved standard host information and already entered arrangement fields. Check native email and calendar templates first. Missing or conflicting details are resolved with the host before final approval.

s1 is a human conversation with a permitted contact, not an automated outreach campaign. s4 approves the complete message and booking before either action; edits require reapproval. No inferred contact permission or mass solicitation is proposed.
research_questions: Does sharing captured arrangement fields reduce re-entry without shortening host discussion?

already_counted.description: Approve final host message and party booking

incremental.description: Maintain templates and reconcile changed party details

approvals.approved_version: Exact host message, arrangements and host recipient approved in s4; changes void delivery approval
Exact date, time, venue, host and booking terms approved in s4; changes void calendar approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes six repeated-drafting and ten send/booking-entry hours less two upkeep. Low assumes existing templates and native bookings already cover the mechanics, leaving upkeep only. Host solicitation and arrangement discussion retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use native mobile sales tools for lookup and records while preserving customer-facing work.
role.ambitious_version: Capture accurate orders and payments once while keeping demonstration, delivery and host relationships human.
